h1: Hot water looks milky or cloudy
title: Hot water looks milky or cloudy | G3 Cylinder Help
description: Understand hot water looks milky or cloudy. Distinguish the symptom, gather useful details and arrange competent cylinder assessment in London.
answer: In an applicable Megaflo, cloudiness that clears can be caused by aeration. Persistent colour, particles or unusual smell need separate investigation.

sections.heading: What this symptom can mean
paragraphs: The manufacturer describes oxygen bubbles released when pressurised water flows. That explanation should not be used to dismiss every water-quality concern or unexplained change in drinking-water appearance.

sections.heading: Information to gather safely
paragraphs: Describe whether the cloudiness clears after standing and whether cold water is also affected. Do not treat visible particles or a lasting colour as the same harmless effect.

sections.heading: How the enquiry becomes an investigation
paragraphs: The cylinder make, full model and heating arrangement should be identified first. The same visible symptom can arise from different causes, and a relief device may be protecting the system rather than creating the original problem. Component testing and any repair belong to a person competent for the work.

sections.heading: Discuss the appropriate next step
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the postcode, symptom history and any previous service findings. The enquiry establishes the proposed assessment and availability. Do not use this guide as a substitute for the actual appliance safety instructions or an on-site diagnosis.

faqs.question: When might milky-looking Megaflo water be aeration rather than a fault?
faqs.answer: Aeration can create temporary cloudiness that clears on standing; persistent discolouration, particles or unusual smell warrant a separate water-quality enquiry.
